title: The diagonal of an affine formal algebraic space is representable and a closed immersion
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: For an affine formal algebraic space X over a scheme, the lemma asserts that its diagonal is representable and a closed immersion (statement lines 2009-2015). The proof tests representability against a pair of morphisms from schemes: writing the space as a filtered colimit of affine schemes, the earlier discussion shows that Zariski locally on the two test schemes the morphisms factor through one of the stages, and on such a piece the fibre product over the space is the fibre product over that stage, which is a scheme; representability of the diagonal follows (proof lines 2017-2026). For the closed immersion one takes a morphism from a scheme into the product of the space with itself, notes again that locally its two components factor through a single stage, and thereby identifies the fibre product with the space along the diagonal as a base change of the diagonal of that affine stage, which is a closed immersion because the stage is separated over the base scheme (proof lines 2028-2037). The claim is H2: one localisation argument is used twice, once for representability and once for the closed immersion property, and in the second case it is combined with the separatedness of an affine scheme over the base.
